title: Validate Binary Search Tree
prompt:
Decide whether a binary tree is a valid binary search tree (BST): for every node, every value in its left subtree is strictly smaller, and every value in its right subtree is strictly larger. Duplicates are not allowed.

Write isValidBST(root). Helpers TreeNode, fromArray, toArray are at the top; keep them.

  • isValidBST(fromArray([2, 1, 3])) returns true
  • isValidBST(fromArray([5, 1, 4, null, null, 3, 6])) returns false (4 is in 5's right subtree but smaller than 5)
  • isValidBST(fromArray([5, 4, 6, null, null, 3, 7])) returns false: each parent-child pair looks fine, but 3 sits in 5's right subtree
  • isValidBST(null) returns true

Constraints: 0 to 104 nodes; values can be negative. Target: O(n).

tests.name: grandchild breaks an ancestor bound
tests.code: assertEqual(isValidBST(fromArray([5, 4, 6, null, null, 3, 7])), false, '3 is in the right subtree of 5; checking only parent vs child misses this');

tests.name: empty and single node are valid
left grandchild too large
tests.code: assertEqual(isValidBST(fromArray([10, 5, 15, 2, 12])), false, '12 is in the left subtree of 10');

hints: Trigger: "is it a valid BST?" Comparing a node only with its direct children is the classic trap. Each node must respect all its ancestors.

Pass a range down. The root can be anything: (-Infinity, Infinity). Going left from a node with value v, the allowed range becomes (low, v). Going right, (v, high). A node outside its range means invalid.

Shape:

function check(node, low, high) {
  if (node === null) return true;
  if (node.val <= low || node.val >= high) return false;
  return check(node.left, low, node.val) && check(node.right, node.val, high);
}
return check(root, -Infinity, Infinity);

(Alternative: an in-order traversal of a BST visits values in strictly increasing order.)
explain:
Time O(n): each node is checked once. Space O(h) call stack. The range is the "extra information" each recursive call needs from above; many tree problems are solved by deciding what to pass down (bounds, a running sum, the depth) and what to return up (a height, a boolean, a count).

Say it: "A local parent-child check isn't enough, so I'll pass down a valid range. Left children tighten the upper bound, right children the lower bound. O(n) time, O(h) space. An in-order traversal that must be strictly increasing also works."
